weight_management: Eat slowly and mindfully to help recognize satiety cues.
Avoid sugary beverages — choose water, herbal tea, or coconut water.
Don't skip meals; focus on portion control instead.
Include a 10-minute walk after meals to aid digestion.
Prioritize 7–9 hours of quality sleep — poor sleep can increase hunger hormones.
general_wellness: Practice gratitude journaling for 5 minutes each morning.
Spend at least 20 minutes outdoors daily for Vitamin D.
Limit screen time before bed by at least 60 minutes.
Stay socially connected — meaningful relationships support mental health.
Practice deep breathing or meditation for 10 minutes daily.
fitness: Progressive overload: gradually increase workout intensity each week.
Fuel your workout with a light snack 30–60 minutes before.
Rest is part of training — schedule 1–2 recovery days per week.
Track your workouts to see progress and stay motivated.
Warm up for 5 minutes before every workout.
strength: Consume protein within 30–45 minutes post-workout for optimal muscle recovery.
Progressive overload is key — add weight or reps each week.
Compound movements (squats, deadlifts, bench press) give the most benefit.
Get 8+ hours of sleep — growth hormone is released during sleep.
Creatine monohydrate is one of the most researched safe supplements.
flexibility: Stretch when muscles are warm, not cold.
Consistency beats intensity — daily gentle stretching is better than occasional intense sessions.
Breathe into each stretch; never force a stretch through pain.
Yoga and foam rolling complement each other well.
Include both static and dynamic stretching in your routine.

menstruation.label: Menstruation Phase
generalSuggestions: Stay well-hydrated — aim for at least 2.5 liters of water.
Warm herbal teas (ginger, chamomile) may help with comfort.
Gentle movement like walking or yoga is generally well-tolerated.
Iron-rich foods (spinach, dal, legumes) support healthy iron levels.
Heating pads may provide soothing comfort for cramping.
Rest is important — listen to your body's energy signals.
menstruation.note: These are general wellness suggestions, not medical advice.

follicular.label: Follicular Phase
generalSuggestions: Energy typically increases during this phase.
A good time to try more challenging workouts.
Focus on nutrient-dense foods rich in antioxidants.
Stay hydrated to support natural energy levels.
follicular.note: These are general wellness suggestions, not medical advice.

ovulation.label: Ovulation Phase
generalSuggestions: Peak energy phase — you may feel most energetic now.
Good time for social activities and high-intensity workouts.
Focus on whole foods and complex carbohydrates for sustained energy.
Stay well-hydrated.
ovulation.note: These are general wellness suggestions, not medical advice.

luteal.label: Luteal Phase
generalSuggestions: Energy may start to decrease toward end of this phase.
Include magnesium-rich foods (nuts, seeds, dark chocolate) for mood support.
Reduce caffeine and salt to minimize bloating.
Prioritize sleep and rest.
Gentle yoga and walking are helpful for mood regulation.
If experiencing unusual symptoms, consult a qualified healthcare professional.
luteal.note: These are general wellness suggestions, not medical advice.

childWellnessFocus: Balanced nutrition with all food groups — grains, protein, dairy, fruits, vegetables.
60+ minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per day (WHO recommendation).
Limit screen time to 2 hours/day for ages 6–12.
8–12 hours of sleep depending on age.
Outdoor play supports physical, mental, and social development.
Encourage variety in food rather than restricting specific foods.
Hydration: about 1.5–2 liters of water per day (age-dependent).
Never use food as a reward or punishment.
Family meals support healthy eating habits.
Regular health check-ups with a qualified pediatrician.
